source.document: AISC, Companion to the AISC Steel Construction Manual, Volume 1: Design Examples, Version 16.0 (2023), accompanying ANSI/AISC 360-22
source.pages: printed page D-n = PDF page 36+n; E-n = PDF page 64+n; G-n = PDF page 236+n; F-n = PDF page 162+n
source.content: Only numbers are recorded here: the inputs each example lists and the values it prints (3 significant figures). No text, table or figure of the document is reproduced.
source.units: kip, in. (ksi); lengths given in ft in the examples are converted in the tests

tolerancePolicy.statement: ONE policy for every comparison with a printed Design Examples value (nominal and available strengths, and the printed intermediates that are compared): the engine value, computed at full precision from the inputs the example lists, must be within 1.0 % of the printed value. The examples print 3 significant figures and carry rounded intermediates into the next step. The tolerance is never adjusted per case; a case that does not meet it is marked xfail(strict) with a diagnosis.

D.1.title: W-shape tension member (W8x21)
notes: Yielding strengths are printed as Manual Table 5-1 values (the example does not print Fy Ag).
An = 4.76 in.^2 (Spec. B4.3b, four holes) and U = 0.908 (Table D3.1 Case 2) are computed in the example from the connection and are INPUTS of the engine.
Rounded chain: printed ASD rupture 141 = 281/2.00; full precision from the listed inputs gives 140.5.

D.4.title: Rectangular HSS tension member (HSS6x4x3/8)
notes: Yielding strengths are printed as Manual Table 5-4 values.
An = 5.79 in.^2 (slot with 1/16 in. gap) and U = 0.919 (Table D3.1 Case 5) are INPUTS of the engine.

D.5.title: Round HSS tension member (HSS6.000x0.500)
notes: Yielding strengths are printed as Manual Table 5-6 values.

E.1C.title: W-shape available compressive strength (W14x132, Lc = 30 ft)
notes: The example takes the available stresses (23.0 and 15.4 ksi) from Manual Table 4-14 by interpolation; Fn is not printed.

Documented printed inconsistency: Eq. E3-2 with the listed properties gives Pn/Omega = 594 kips (the value Example E.1A quotes from Manual Table 4-1a for the same member); the printed 598 follows from the interpolated 15.4 ksi. The difference (0.6 %) is inside the policy.

E.1D.title: W-shape available compressive strength (W14x90, Lcx = 30 ft, Lcy = Lcz = 15 ft)
notes: Torsional buckling is not evaluated in the example; J and Cw are not listed.

E.1E.title: W-shape compression member with slender elements (W16x31)
notes: Flexural buckling only (problem statement); Lc is the same about both axes, so the minor axis governs.
Case b: the example rounds Lc/r to 103 before squaring (printed 210/189/126; Manual Table 6-1 values printed alongside: 190/127); full precision gives 211.5/190.4/126.7.

E.2.title: Built-up column with a slender web
notes: Section properties (Ag, Ix, Iy, ry, Cw, J) are computed in the example from the plate dimensions and listed; they are used as inputs here.

E.3.title: Built-up column with slender flanges
notes: The flange is slender by Table B4.1a but fully effective at this Fn (Eq. E7-2): Ae = Ag.

E.9.title: Rectangular HSS compression member without slender elements (HSS12x10x3/8)
notes: Lc = 0.80 x 20 ft about both axes; the design wall thickness is not listed (only b/t and h/t).

E.10.title: Rectangular HSS compression member with slender elements (HSS12x8x3/16)
notes: Flat widths are taken in the example as (ratio) x t: h = 66.0 x 0.174, b = 43.0 x 0.174.
The 18 ft and 40 ft columns are given only in the summary table of the example.

E.11.title: Pipe compression member (Pipe 10 Std.)
notes: The hand calculation (221/147) differs from the Manual Table 4-6 values quoted in the same example (222/148) by rounding.

G.1B.title: W-shape in major-axis shear (W24x62)
notes: The example does not print h/tw: it states that Section G2.1(a) applies (Cv1 = 1.0, phi = 1.00, Omega = 1.50). The test supplies h/tw equal to the limit 2.24 sqrt(E/Fy), the largest value for which that statement holds; the result does not depend on h/tw below the limit.
Vu and Va are those of Example G.1A (G-3).

G.4.title: Rectangular HSS in shear (HSS6x4x3/8, 6-in. walls vertical)
notes: Rounded chain: 93.6 and 62.3 follow from Vn rounded to 104; full precision gives 103.7, 93.3, 62.1.

G.5.title: Round HSS in shear (HSS16.000x0.375)
notes: Documented printed inconsistency: 258/1.67 = 154.49, which rounds to 154; the example prints 155. The difference (0.3 %) is inside the policy.
Lv = half the 32 ft span (simply supported, uniform load).

G.6.title: Doubly symmetric shape in minor-axis shear (W21x48)

G.8B.title: Built-up girder with transverse stiffeners: web shear buckling coefficient Cv2 of the second panel
notes: Only the coefficient of Eq. G2-11 is reproduced: the example goes on with the tension-field strength of Eq. G2-7, which the engine does not implement.
kv = 5.67 and h/tw = 106 are the rounded values the example carries into Eq. G2-11; kv is also recomputed from a and h (Eq. G2-5).

F.3B.title: W-shape with noncompact flanges, major-axis bending (W21x48): classification only
notes: Only the Table B4.1b classification is used here (the flexural strength belongs to Chapter F).
The web ratio is not printed in the example.

F.7B.title: Rectangular HSS with noncompact flanges (HSS10x6x3/16, major axis): classification only
notes: Only the Table B4.1b classification is used here.

F.9B.title: Pipe flexural member: classification only
notes: Only the Table B4.1b classification is used here.
